question: Are islands, curbs, speed humps, raised roadway surfaces, and rumble strips considered traffic control devices under the MUTCD?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The MUTCD explicitly states (as Support/explanatory text) that islands, curbs, speed humps, other raised roadway surfaces, and transverse or longitudinal rumble strips are not traffic control devices. This is consistent with the normative definition of traffic control devices, which covers signs, signals, markings, channelizing devices, and other devices whose primary purpose is communicating a message to road users. Standards (mandatory): - "Traffic control devices shall be defined as all signs, signals, markings, channelizing devices, or other devices that use colors, shapes, symbols, words, sounds, or tactile information for the primary purpose of communicating a regulatory, warning, or guidance message to road users on a street, highway, pedestrian facility, bikeway, pathway, or site roadway open to public travel." - "The Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices for Streets and Highways (MUTCD)... shall be recognized as the national standard for all traffic control devices installed on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel." Support (informational, not normative): - "Infrastructure elements that restrict the road user's travel paths or vehicle speeds, such as islands, curbs, speed humps, and other raised roadway surfaces, are not traffic control devices. Transverse or longitudinal rumble strips are also not traffic control devices." Related operational devices (fencing, roadway lighting, barriers, attenuators) are shown in the Manual only for context. - "Although they are not considered to be traffic control devices, raised islands (see Chapter 3J) are also sometimes used to channelize traffic." Citations: - Section 1A.02 Support §2 (p.1) - Section 3I.01 Support §2 (p.632) - Section 6A.03 Standard §2 (p.768) - Section 1B.01 Standard §1 (p.4)
gold_answer: No. Infrastructure elements that physically restrict travel paths or speeds, including islands, curbs, speed humps, other raised surfaces, and transverse or longitudinal rumble strips, are not traffic control devices.
